blindSummary:
This country carries moderate but real risk, with several documented traveler-axis dangers and a long-running government hostility climate. The most severe traveler-specific finding: two young transgender tourists were raped, and the convictions were confirmed on appeal in April 2026. Organised dating-app entrapment gangs have also been prosecuted (a dating-app-lure robbery gang prosecuted in one city; a 2025 assault in another).

There is documented police violence toward trans people: a municipal police officer was convicted in 2024 for beating a trans woman with batons in 2023. If arrested, trans women are placed in male prisons on the basis of biological sex, mitigated by a specialized section in one capital-city prison. The current national government has run openly hostile rhetoric toward LGBT people for years — attacking the "LGBT lobby" and "gender ideology", and criminalising surrogacy abroad — and the country is rated among the least progressive in its region on LGBT policy.

The major tourist cities have established queer scenes and are generally safe day-to-day; bathrooms are unrestricted and there is no cross-dressing statute.
blindOutOfScope: Pickpocketing and counterfeit-goods fines affect all tourists; no trans-specific travel advisory.
blindSourceSummaries: National news agency (April 2026): convictions confirmed on appeal for the violent assault of trans tourists in one region - shows judicial response to violence against trans visitors.

Regional LGBTI-rights organisation annual review 2026 (covering 2025), chapter on this country: the education ministry omitted LGBTI persecution from the circulars for a national memorial day of historical atrocities for a second year; a senior church figure called homosexual acts 'a mortal sin'; homophobic and transphobic violence continued including organised dating-app entrapment schemes targeting gay men; in March a provincial civil court recognised for the first time physical and psychological harm from homophobic mistreatment.

Research-institute national report (July 2025) on LGBTIQ detainees in this country: an overview of discrimination and violence against LGBTIQ prisoners, pathways to gender affirmation, same-sex relationships, and the legal/policy framework for LGBTIQ people in detention.

International human-rights organisation world report 2025, chapter on this country: the right-wing governing coalition pursued offshore asylum processing and obstructed sea rescues; parliament criminalised seeking surrogacy abroad; harmful policies and rhetoric about LGBT people contributed to a hostile environment (sexual orientation and gender identity section).

News outlet (July 2024): a municipal police officer was sentenced to 10 months (accelerated procedure) for aggravated assault on a 43-year-old trans woman beaten with batons and pepper-sprayed in May 2023; two other officers and the victim herself face trial.

A religious LGBT-ministry project: article describing transphobia in this country as 'the most atrocious and widespread discrimination against transgender people' - a faith-community perspective on discrimination.

International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): one of the least progressive countries in its region - civil unions but no adoption (stepchild adoption only via lengthy judicial procedure); an October 2024 law classifies surrogacy as a crime punishable wherever committed, with extraterritorial penalties; employment discrimination banned on sexual orientation only, no nationwide SOGIESC protections (some regions have broader laws); legal gender change requires a gender-dysphoria diagnosis and court approval.
